auxiliary_material: The study details the molecular mechanism (inosine-A2AR-cAMP-CREB signaling) and the context-dependency of inosine effects (requiring co-stimulation like IL-12/IFN-γ). It also reports differential efficacy of the bacterial-metabolite circuit across different colorectal cancer subtypes in mouse models (effective in MMRD and inflammation-associated models, ineffective in APC/KRAS models). These findings support the biological rationale for measuring these metabolites but do not address measurement standardization.
outline_action: Search for methodological papers or consensus statements from clinical metabolomics organizations regarding standard operating procedures for absolute quantification of inosine and short-chain fatty acids in human serum or tissue. Look for validation studies that compare measurement platforms or establish reference ranges for these metabolites in human populations.
remaining_gap: The success criteria require consensus guidelines or widely adopted methodological papers for standardized measurement of absolute metabolite concentrations in human tumor microenvironment or serum. This study provides experimental concentration data derived exclusively from mouse models (germ-free, SPF, monocolonized) using specific metabolomics facilities, without describing a standardized protocol applicable to human clinical samples or citing a consensus guideline for such measurements.
useful_material: This study investigated the mechanism by which gut microbiota enhance immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in colorectal cancer using mouse models. The authors identified inosine as a critical bacterial metabolite that promotes Th1 cell differentiation via the A2A receptor. They quantified absolute inosine concentrations in mouse serum and intestinal contents using untargeted metabolomics and fragmentation analysis (e.g., serum inosine in B.p. monocolonized mice was 26.16 ± 3.32µM; duodenal content was 66.13 ±14.23 µM). This material helps the gap by confirming that inosine is a quantifiable metabolite of interest and providing example concentration ranges in a biological system, demonstrating the feasibility of measuring absolute levels (µM) in serum and tissue contexts.
